newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PACDUN MULLS FUTURE OF PAY-TV CABLE PLANT.
newsitem.headline: PACDUN MULLS FUTURE OF PAY-TV CABLE PLANT.

text.p: Pacific Dunlop said on Monday it is looking at options for its joint venture coaxial cable plant in Melbourne which will suspend production in August due to a slow-down in Australia's pay television cable roll-out.

On Friday, U.S.-based Commscope Inc, 49 percent partner in the Vision Cables venture which owns the plant, said it may need to post a loss on the venture of between US$1 million and US$3 million if operations are permanently discontinued.
"We have only just been informed of the forward forecasts for cable. It's true it (the slow-down) is earlier than we would have expected," a spokesman from Pacific Dunlop told Reuters.
The spokesman said cable is becoming a maintenance market in Australia which could be served by imports of CommScope cable product.

The Vision Cables plant started production in 1995. It supplies coaxial cable to government-owned Telstra Corp for its Foxtel pay-TV joint venture with News Corp, and to Optus Vision, which is owned by Telstra's main competitor Optus Communications Pty Ltd.
Optus is 49 percent owned by Britain's Cable & Wireless.
Australia's pay-tv operators have recently scaled-down their cable roll-out programmes dramatically due to large losses experienced by the industry.
